2. M.F.A. No.103423/2022 is filed by claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, whereas, M.F.A. No.105031/2019 is filed by the insurance company seeking reduction of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties in the present appeals are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petition.

4. Brief facts of the claimants' case before the Tribunal are as under:
 On 19.09.2017 at about 07:00 a.m., the deceased Ravikumar and his brother i.e., respondent No.1 were in their  -6-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:18040-DB  MFA No. 103423 of 2022  C/W MFA No. 105031 of 2019 land for doing agricultural operation by using the tractor bearing No.KA-37/TB-2365.
At that time, the said vehicle was not moving due to wet land.

When said Ravikumar was trying to push the said tractor from the backside and the respondent No.1 was driving the said tractor, but suddenly the respondent No.1 has drove the said vehicle in high speed and negligent Smt. Laxmi W/O Ravikumar Y vs Sri Jagadish Y S/O Hanumappa Y on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5792788/
5 manner and given accelerator and due to such negligent driving of respondent No.1, tractor turtled down and fell on deceased Ravikumar due to which he has sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries at the spot.

5. The claimants being the wife, children and mother of the deceased, filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, awarded a sum of Rs.55,77,712/-.
Aggrieved by the same, the insurer of the offending vehicle as well as the claimants have filed these appeals.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties in both the appeals.

7. Learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the Tribunal committed an error in deducting the income of the deceased as Rs.27,320/- per month without properly considering the income tax returns produced by the claimants.
It has been sated in the income tax return that there is no income from the agriculture.
However, the Tribunal taken the income without properly studying all the documents.
The Tribunal considering Ex.P10 taken the income for the year 2017-18 as Rs.3,27,850/- which is not in accordance with law.

Further, the learned counsel contended that the accident Smt. Laxmi W/O Ravikumar Y vs Sri Jagadish Y S/O Hanumappa Y on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5792788/
6 occurred in a private place and if the accident has happened in a private place, the petition under Section 166 of the Act is not maintainable and there is no charge sheet under Section 279 of the IPC.

sentences.text: On these grounds, the learned counsel for the insurance company sought to allow the appeal filed by the insurance company.
Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side.
The Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium to claimant No.1 alone.
In fact, there are four claimants.
Hence, all are entitled for the compensation under the head loss of consortium.

Further, the Tribunal has not properly awarded compensation under the head loss of dependency considering the materials available on record i.e.,
the income tax returns.
Hence, the learned counsel prayed to enhance the compensation suitably.

9. In view of the contentions urged by both the learned counsels for the parties, the following point that would Smt. Laxmi W/O Ravikumar Y vs Sri Jagadish Y S/O Hanumappa Y on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5792788/

 "i.
Whether the quantum of compensation  awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or  does it call for any enhancement or reduction?"
10. The insurance company has taken a contention that the accident occurred in a private place and the Investigating Officer has not filed charge sheet for the offences under Sections 279 of IPC.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
Perused the evidence and Ex.P1 - RIR, Ex.P2 - complaint, Ex.P3 - panchanama and Ex.P6 - charge sheet.

From the perusal of these documents, it clearly establishes that on 19.09.2017 at about 07:00 a.m. deceased Ravikumar and his brother were in their land for doing agricultural operation by using the tractor bearing No.KA-37/TB-2365.
At that time, the said vehicle was not moving due to wet land.

When said Ravikumar was trying to push the said tractor from the backside and the respondent No.1 was driving the said tractor,
but suddenly the respondent No.1 has drove the said vehicle in high speed and negligent manner and given accelerator and due to such negligent driving of respondent No.1, tractor turtled down and fell on deceased Ravikumar.

In this regard,
the matter was investigating and the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Section 304A of Smt. Laxmi W/O Ravikumar Y vs Sri Jagadish Y S/O Hanumappa Y on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5792788/
8 the IPC.
Therefore, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the tractor.
12. So far as quantum is concerned, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.39,34,080/- considering the monthly income as Rs.27,320/-.

To substantive the claim of the claimants, the claimant No.1 examined on oath as PW1 and  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:18040-DB  MFA No. 103423 of 2022  C/W MFA No. 105031 of 2019 relied upon in all Exs.P1 to P10.

From the perusal of Exs.P8 to P10 - the income tax returns, the deceased's income for the assessment years 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 is for a sum of Rs.2,86,730/-, Rs.2,94,930/- and Rs.3,27,850/-
respectively, total Rs.9,09,510/-.
The learned counsel for the insurance company has taken contention that the Tribunal has not deducted income tax for the relevant period.

Accordingly,
the income tax and the professional tax paid for the relevant period are Rs.7,652/-[Rs.2,012/-, Rs.2,743/- and Rs.2,897/-],
and Rs.7,200/- [Rs.2,400 X 3] respectively, total Rs.14,852/- [Rs.7,652 + Rs.7,200].
After deducting the income tax and the professional tax, the average income would come to Rs.8,94,658/- [Rs.9,09,510 - Rs.14,852].

If we take the average income of the deceased per annum, then the same comes to Rs.2,98,219/- [Rs.8,94,658  3].
 13.

There is no dispute with regard to adding 40%

9 towards future prospects, 16 multiplier based on the age group of the deceased at the time of the accident and 1/4th deduction towards personal expenses of the deceased [as there are four claimants].

Thus, loss of dependency is reckoned as under:
 - 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:18040-DB  MFA No. 103423 of 2022  C/W MFA No. 105031 of 2019  Rs.2,98,219 + 40% X 16 -  = Rs.50,10,080/-
 14.

So far as compensation under the head loss of consortium, the Tribunal has granted only a sum of Rs.40,000/-
and in view of the National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others1 and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram2, claimant Nos.1 to 4, who are the wife, daughters and mother of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,60,000/-
towards loss of consortium.

However, in view of the decision in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others vs.

Loss of dependency Rs.50,10,080/-
Loss of consortium [Rs.40,000 x 4] Rs.1,60,000/-
Loss of estate 15,000/-
Funeral expenses 15,000/-

. Thus, the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.52,00,080/- as against Rs.40,04,080/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
19 . Accordingly, the point for consideration is answered partly in the affirmative.

In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER i.
Both the appeals are allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.52,00,080/- as against Rs.40,04,080/- awarded by the Tribunal.

the matter was investigating and the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Section 304A of Smt. Laxmi W/O Ravikumar Y vs Sri Jagadish Y S/O Hanumappa Y on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5792788/
8 the IPC.
Therefore, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the tractor.
12. So far as quantum is concerned, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.39,34,080/- considering the monthly income as Rs.27,320/-.
So far as compensation under the head loss of consortium, the Tribunal has granted only a sum of Rs.40,000/-
and in view of the National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others1 and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram2, claimant Nos.1 to 4, who are the wife, daughters and mother of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,60,000/-
towards loss of consortium.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
7. Learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the Tribunal committed an error in deducting the income of the deceased as Rs.27,320/- per month without properly considering the income tax returns produced by the claimants.
It has been sated in the income tax return that there is no income from the agriculture.
However, the Tribunal taken the income without properly studying all the documents.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has erred in awarding interest at 7% per annum and the same has to be reduced to 6% per annum in view of the judgment of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others vs.
Venkateshan.V and others [M.F.A. No.5896/2018 and connected matters disposed off on 24.8.2020].
Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side.
Hence, the learned counsel prayed to enhance the compensation suitably.
opennyai_summary.issue:
are:
 "i.
Whether the quantum of compensation  awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or  does it call for any enhancement or reduction?"
10. The insurance company has taken a contention that the accident occurred in a private place and the Investigating Officer has not filed charge sheet for the offences under Sections 279 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
15. In respect of loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of body is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded just compensation and the same is maintained.
16 . Insofar as interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded 7% interest per annum on the compensation amount appears to be excessive.
17 . Thus, the claimants are entitled for the following modified compensation:
Loss of dependency Rs.50,10,080/-
Loss of consortium [Rs.40,000 x 4] Rs.1,60,000/-
Loss of estate 15,000/-
Funeral expenses 15,000/-
Total Rs.52,00,080/-
 18
. Thus, the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.52,00,080/- as against Rs.40,04,080/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
19 . Accordingly, the point for consideration is answered partly in the affirmative.
In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER i.
Both the appeals are allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.52,00,080/- as against Rs.40,04,080/- awarded by the Tribunal.

11 NC: 2024:KHC-D:18040-DB iii.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
iv. Respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v. Apportionment, disbursement and deposit shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
vi. The amount in deposit, if any, before this Court shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
vii. Draw modified award accordingly.
viii.
Registry is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
